passage:
Asif: are you awake
Karthik: yeah, what happened
Asif: I need to tell you something and you can't laugh
Karthik: ok. not laughing
Asif: someone called and said I'd won a phone. I paid a "delivery fee" through a link
Asif: then they asked for more for "customs". I paid that too, two days ago
Asif: I told nobody. I thought you'd all say I'm stupid
Karthik: they run this on hundreds of people, Asif. Have you told your bank?
Asif: no. Every day I waited felt worse. They keep messaging me for more
Karthik: stop replying. Call the bank's helpline now and report it on the cyber crime portal. I'll sit next to you while you do it
Asif: ok. give me ten minutes to find the card

qa.q: What did the caller say Asif had won?
qa.a: The caller said Asif had won a phone.

qa.q: Why did Asif wait two days before telling anyone?
qa.a: Asif feared people would say Asif was stupid, and the messages show that waiting only made each day feel worse.

qa.q: What would you advise Asif to do right now?
qa.a: Stop replying to the scammers, call the bank's helpline, and report it on the cyber crime portal, ideally with Karthik sitting next to Asif. 🤍

qa.q: How does Karthik see what happened to Asif?
qa.a: Karthik sees it as something that happens to hundreds of people, not proof of stupidity, and offers to sit next to Asif while the calls are made.

grounding: Asif hides a scam out of fear of mockery, the silence lets it grow, and speaking up early leads to reporting.

passage: Saturday. Bhavna's diary. Ten days. For ten days I've told nobody that I paid a 'registration fee' to a hostel-booking site that turned out to be fake. Then they asked for a 'refund processing fee', and I paid that too, because I was scared that if I stopped I'd lose the first amount forever. Every time Darshan-bhaiya asked why I looked so tired, I said exams. I couldn't bear him laughing at me. Tonight another message came asking for more, and something in me snapped. I knocked on bhaiya's door and told him everything. He didn't laugh. He said, 'Why didn't you tell me on day one?' and helped me report it on the cyber-crime helpline and call the bank tonight. The bank said reporting sooner might have helped more. That stings. But at least the loop has stopped.

qa.a: Bhavna paid a 'registration fee' to a hostel-booking site.

qa.q: What was Bhavna feeling during the ten days of silence?
qa.a: Bhavna felt scared and ashamed, afraid of losing the first amount and of being laughed at.
The loop stopped: they reported it to the cyber-crime helpline and the bank that same night.

qa.q: How does Darshan-bhaiya react to Bhavna's story?
qa.a: Darshan-bhaiya doesn't laugh; he only wishes Bhavna had told him on day one, and helps at once.

grounding: A diary shows shame keeping a scam secret while the losses grow, and speaking up to family stopping the loop.

passage:
Jagdish: can I tell you something and you promise not to laugh
Farida: promise
Jagdish: someone I met online said they were sending me a gift from abroad. then 'customs' called and said pay a fee to release it
Jagdish: I paid. then they said pay again for 'clearance'
Farida: how many times?
Jagdish: 3. over 2 weeks. I didn't tell anyone. felt like such an idiot
Farida: you're not an idiot. this is a known scam, it happened to my aunt too
Farida: have you reported it?
Jagdish: no. I was hoping they'd just send the parcel
Farida: they won't. the silence is what they count on
Farida: call the cyber-crime helpline now, and your bank. the earlier the better
Jagdish: ok. calling now
Jagdish: done. they gave me a complaint number
Farida: proud of you. block that 'friend' too

qa.q: How many times did Jagdish pay?
What was Jagdish feeling during those two weeks?
qa.a: Jagdish felt ashamed and foolish, too embarrassed to tell anyone.

qa.q: Why did Farida push Jagdish to report straight away?
qa.a: Because scammers rely on silence, and reporting early to the helpline and the bank gives the best chance and stops more payments.

qa.q: How does Farida see Jagdish's mistake?
qa.a: Farida sees it as a known scam that happens to many people, like her aunt, not as foolishness.

grounding: A chat shows a scam kept secret out of shame, and a friend urging Jagdish to report early, block the contact and break the silence scammers rely on.
